citeAs: Wadhawan, R., Bansal, H., Chang, K.-W., and Peng, N. (2024). CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models. Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235.
creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng (University of California Los Angeles)
description: CONTEXTUAL is a context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning dataset consisting of 506 challenging instructions for large multimodal model (LMM) evaluation. It covers eight real-world scenarios with text-rich images: time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes, mobile application, webpages, infographics, and miscellaneous natural scenes. Each instance contains a human-written instruction and a human-written ground-truth response, requiring context-sensitive joint reasoning over textual and visual cues in the image.
name: CONTEXTUAL
rai:annotationsPerItem: For human evaluation: each model response was rated by 3 human annotators independently, with majority vote as final decision. For dataset annotation verification: MTurk workers verified each sample.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Human annotators for the performance baseline were mainly from the US (sourced from Amazon Mechanical Turk). Annotators passed a qualification test before being asked to write accurate responses. The authors acknowledge that annotator demographics affect linguistic diversity and writing style of responses.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: MTurk workers verified 96% of samples were annotated correctly in Stage 3. For human evaluation, majority vote among three annotators was used as the final decision. Correlation analysis between human and automated evaluation metrics was performed using ROC-AUC and Spearman correlation; GPT-4 evaluation achieved the highest ROC-AUC of 85.9 and Spearman correlation of 0.71.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) for verification (Stage 3) and human performance baseline collection
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage annotation process: Stage 1 - image shortlisting with manual filtering for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories, and heuristic-based filtering (PaddleOCR text detection, selecting top 500 images with highest word count) for other categories. Stage 2 - authors divided into two groups, each annotating four categories following strict annotation guidelines. Stage 3 - verification by MTurk workers (mutually exclusive from human baseline and evaluation workers) who verified correctness of each sample; 96% were annotated correctly. Incorrect samples were filtered, and each author group reviewed the other group's samples to ensure guideline adherence and filter low-quality samples.
rai:dataBiases: Human annotators for the baseline were mainly from the US, introducing potential linguistic and cultural bias in human responses and evaluations. The authors acknowledge that linguistic diversity and writing style would change with different social groups. GPT-4V may have been tuned on memes and quotes data, giving it an advantage in the abstract category where it outperforms humans. Open models may underperform on digital scenes due to training data predominantly comprising natural scenes (e.g., COCO dataset).
rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from six different sources: (1) LAION-5B for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories using keyword search via CLIP-retrieval UI; (2) Rico Dataset for Application Usage (66,000 distinct UI screens from 9,300 Android apps); (3) Open WebText Initiative website links for Web Usage screenshots; (4) InfographicVQA dataset for Infographic images; (5) STVQA and ESTVQA datasets for Miscellaneous Natural Scenes. Instructions and responses were human-written by the paper authors following annotation guidelines.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from LAION-5B (via CLIP-retrieval keyword search), Rico Dataset (Android UI screenshots), Open WebText Initiative (web screenshots), InfographicVQA dataset, STVQA dataset, and ESTVQA dataset. These were then annotated with novel human-written instruction-response pairs.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: Human annotators for the baseline were mainly from the US, limiting linguistic and cultural diversity. The dataset covers only English-language text in images. Creating synthetic data for context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning is challenging, as automatic generation tends to produce instructions solvable by OCR+LLM rather than requiring genuine visual context understanding. The dataset size (506 samples) is relatively small compared to other benchmarks.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories: manual filtering of images to guarantee suitability for annotation. For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes: heuristic-based filtering using PaddleOCR to detect text, selecting top 500 images with the highest number of words. Images from existing VQA datasets (InfographicVQA, STVQA, ESTVQA) were re-annotated with novel context-sensitive instruction-response pairs.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance LMM capabilities for real-world applications such as assisting visually impaired individuals in navigating text-rich scenes (e.g., maps in public spaces) and creative understanding of abstract text-rich images (e.g., memes). The authors ensured images, instructions, and responses are not offensive to any social group. Human annotators were mainly from the US, and the authors acknowledge that linguistic diversity and writing style of human responses would change with different social groups, suggesting future work should involve annotators from more diverse regions.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning capabilities of large multimodal models (LMMs); benchmarking foundation models on joint reasoning over embedded text and visual context in images; assessing model performance across diverse real-world visual scenarios including navigation, shopping, time reading, and infographic understanding; supporting development of next-generation LMMs with improved visual perception and reasoning.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: PaddleOCR (PP-OCRv4 model) used for heuristic-based image filtering (detecting text and selecting top 500 images with highest word count); CLIP-retrieval UI used for keyword-based image search from LAION-5B; ShareGPT-4V-7B used for generating dense image captions in augmented LLM experiments; GPT-4V used for synthetic data generation pipeline.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The authors state that qualitative analysis of model responses did not reveal any apparent harmful or privacy-sensitive information. The dataset was designed to avoid offensive content toward any social group.
